blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Fort Langley
The Village at Bedford Landing — 23285 Billy Brown Rd (the same strata plan, EPS998, also covers 23255 Billy Brown Rd)

71 homes in 4 storeys, wood-frame construction, freehold strata, built 2012, managed by Associa, with underground and visitor parking, per a building-data source drawing on MLS and public strata records; a Township page confirms the civic address 23285 Billy Brown Road, Fort Langley.
Waterfront at Bedford Landing — 23215 Billy Brown Rd
Strata plan BCS3620; 4 storeys, built 2009, wood-frame construction with fibre-cement, stone and wood siding, per listing construction details.
Lily Terrace — 23189 Francis Ave

A small low-rise condo building at the east side of the village, built by Lanstone Homes; listings record it as an apartment/condo in a 3-storey building, with sources differing on the year — 2018 in a current listing, 2019 in building records — so the year is best stated as 2018–2019 pending the Form B / depreciation documents.
Streets, schools and getting around Fort Langley

items.t: Fort Langley is a village in the Township of Langley on the south bank of the Fraser River, described by the Township as the birthplace of BC, with its commercial core on Glover Road.

Where the condo stock actually concentrates: in one riverside pocket — Bedford Landing, on Billy Brown Road along the Bedford Channel, west of the Glover Road village core. Two of the village's three verified apartment-condo buildings are there, a few hundred metres apart. The third, Lily Terrace, is on Francis Avenue at the village's east side, steps from the Glover Road shops.

There are no condo towers in Fort Langley, and no high-rise is contemplated by the village framework: the downtown core is a designated Heritage Conservation Area, and new development must complement the heritage character.
Glover Road is the village commercial street holding the shops; Lee's Market, the village grocery, is at 23320 Mavis Avenue, and there is no shopping centre in Fort Langley.

Transit is a single bus: TransLink route 562 runs through the village on Glover Road between Langley Centre and Carvolth Exchange, via Walnut Grove. There is no SkyTrain or West Coast Express station in Fort Langley.

SD35 schools physically in the village are Fort Langley Elementary (8877 Bartlett St) and Langley Fine Arts School (9096 Trattle St), a district K-12 fine arts choice school; a locator run for 8877 Bartlett St returned Fort Langley Elementary and D.W. Poppy Secondary, with no middle school shown, and catchments are address-based.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Fort Langley

items.t: Village plan: the Fort Langley Community Plan, Township of Langley Bylaw No. 2527: (adopted October 26, 1987, as an amendment to the Township Official Community Plan), is the governing plan for the village.

Heritage Conservation Area: That plan designates a Heritage Conservation Area under the Local Government Act covering the downtown core (added by Bylaw 3710, October 27, 1997), to protect the heritage character of downtown Fort Langley; non-exempt work requires approval under the heritage rules, with exemptions including minor additions under 50 m² that do not front a road (other than a lane) and conform to the guidelines. Condo buyers should note this governs exteriors and common-property alterations near the core, on top of strata approval.

Design controls on top of zoning: The village is also covered by a Development Permit Area (Bylaw 3204, May 3, 1993) and the Fort Langley Design Guidelines (Bylaw 5063, April 28, 2014); the separate Building Façade Design Guidelines are non-binding policy.

Zoning: Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw No. 2500: applies in the village; Residential Zone R-1E is named for the village in a Township public-hearing document, and minimum lot areas/frontages for the village zones are not verified from a readable bylaw section.

SSMUH in the Township: Bylaw No. 6020, adopted November 18, 2024, amended Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 to enable small-scale multi-unit housing in most zones previously restricted to single-family or duplex dwellings. In Fort Langley it operates inside the heritage and design controls above — SSMUH permission is not an exemption from a Heritage Conservation Area or development permit requirement.

Flood — a condo issue here, not just a house issue: Fort Langley is low-lying: the Township states the Salmon River Pump Station provides flood protection for the Fort Langley community and its flood box gates close when Fraser River levels rise. Parcel-level floodplain status for a specific building: Not verified — get it from the Township, and check the strata's insurance summary on the Form B for flood coverage and deductible terms.

Presales and assignments — REDMA: Any Fort Langley presale requires a disclosure statement and carries a 7-day rescission right from the later of signing or acknowledging receipt of it; deposits are held in trust or covered by deposit protection insurance, and assignment rights are contract-specific.

CMHC premium range: 0.60% of the loan at 65% loan-to-value or less, to 4.00% at 90.01%–95%, and 4.50% in that band with a non-traditional down payment; a one-time premium that may be added to the loan.

blocks.text: Good to know about Fort Langley

items.t: The newest village housing project is a heritage restoration, not a condo building. The 1912, by Lanstone Homes (the same builder as Lily Terrace), is a presale collection of three heritage-inspired townhomes plus the restored 1912 George Albion Towle House, with pre-sales stated as coming Winter 2027 and move-in Fall 2027 — developer-stated timing, and a townhouse product, so it does not add to the village's condo count.

salishan Place by the River changed the village's civic core. The Township's arts, culture and heritage facility at 23430 Mavis Avenue — developed in partnership with the Katzie, Kwantlen, Matsqui and Semiahmoo First Nations — now houses both the Fort Langley Community Library and the museum, a short walk from the Bedford Landing condos.

Flood protection is being upgraded, and it is a Township project, not a strata one. The Township states the Salmon River Pump Station provides flood protection for Fort Langley, with flood box gates that close as Fraser River levels rise, and Council has authorized staff to proceed with detailed design and tendering for pump station upgrades. Ask what phase that work is in when you buy — it affects the village, not your building's own systems.

Bedford Landing is a mill site turned neighbourhood. The community was built on the grounds of the McDonald Cedar Mill, which opened in 1921 on an 88-acre riverfront property, and its restored pump house and replicated boom-crane wharf remain on the waterfront; the Fort-to-Fort Trail runs about 8 km round trip through Bedford Landing along the river. That history is why the condo buildings sit in a planned riverside enclave rather than on the Glover Road grid.

A March 2026 Township SSMUH step touches Fort Langley specifically. The Township's March 9, 2026 council report on an SSMUH development permit area names the Fort Langley Community Plan among the plans Bylaw No. 6116 would amend — meaning the form-and-character rules for new small-scale multi-unit housing in the village were still being written in 2026, inside the existing heritage framework.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Fort Langley
Leah (Lēah) — 9122 King Street. Freehold strata
Rental restrictions: none may be enforced for long-term rentals in any case; no age restriction appears in the developer's description or any source checked — it is not 55+ stock.
Flatiron (Bedford Landing) — 23230 Billy Brown Road. Freehold strata

A listing for a unit in the complex describes a "well run 11 unit complex — live/work built by Parklane," a 2-storey-with-basement townhouse form, Year Built 2012, Building Name: Flatiron, Ownership Type: Freehold Strata, strata restrictions: pets allowed with restrictions. The live/work designation is the diligence item: permitted business use, signage and any Township licence sit in the strata bylaws, the CD zoning and the unit's permitted-use documents, not in the listing. Rental/age restrictions beyond the pet line: Not confirmed.
Bedford Landing row homes — Billy Brown Road (the 23000 block, Bedford Landing). FEE-SIMPLE (non-strata)

Listing records for homes in this stock classify them as Property Type: Townhouse, Dwelling Type: Row House (Non-Strata), Complex Name: Bedford Landing, built 2007 — attached row homes on their own fee-simple lots, with no strata corporation, no strata fee and no Form B. This is a housing-form grouping within the Bedford Landing master community, not a single named complex; unit count for the row-home stock as a whole: Not confirmed — no source checked publishes it. Bedford Landing as a whole is a mixed community of houses, row homes, townhomes, live/work townhomes and apartments/condos on the former McDonald Cedar Mill lands, so the tenure must be read address by address — the strata buildings and the fee-simple rows share a community name.
Streets, schools and getting around Fort Langley

items.t: Where the townhouse stock actually concentrates: two pockets — Bedford Landing on Billy Brown Road along the Bedford Channel, west of the Glover Road core (fee-simple row homes plus the Flatiron live/work townhouses), and King Street in the village heart (Leah). The 1912 presale will add three more townhomes at village scale.

There are no townhouse towers and no large townhouse subdivisions in Fort Langley, and the village framework works against them: the downtown core is a designated Heritage Conservation Area, and new development must complement the heritage character.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Fort Langley

items.t: Two tenures, two diligence tracks — this sub-area has both: For the strata complexes (Leah, Flatiron): Form B, bylaws, depreciation report and CRF, per the bullets below. For the fee-simple Bedford Landing row homes: no strata, no Form B and no strata fees — municipal rules (Zoning Bylaw No. 2500, the Community Plan, heritage/design controls) plus any registered covenants or building scheme on title govern instead. Confirm which track a Billy Brown Road address is on before drafting subjects; the community name does not tell you. (Complex entries in above.)

Form B first (strata stock): The Form B Information Certificate discloses a unit's monthly strata fees, amounts owed, approved special levies still to be paid, the contingency reserve fund (CRF) balance, parking/storage, and a summary of the strata's insurance; the strata must provide it within 7 days of a request, for a maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.

Depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle (strata stock): Since July 1, 2024, every BC strata with five or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every five years, with 30-year projections and at least three CRF funding models, non-deferrable by vote. Both Leah (2024) and Flatiron (2012) are over that lot threshold on their verified counts.
CRF minimum 10% (strata stock): Since November 1, 2023, a strata's annual budget must contribute at least 10% of the operating fund to the contingency reserve fund.

Rental-restriction bylaws are void (strata stock): As of Nov 24, 2022, no BC strata may have a residential rental-restriction bylaw; any directory line saying "rentals not allowed" for Leah or Flatiron is void for long-term rentals. Short-term rentals may still be restricted by bylaw. Fee-simple row homes carry no strata rental bylaw at all — rental limits there, if any, come from title covenants and Township bylaws.

Age bylaws: 55+ is the only legal form (strata stock): Under the Strata Property Act, ss. 123.1 and 123.2, a strata may restrict residents to 55 or older; bylaws set below 55 have been invalid since Nov 24, 2022, with exemptions expanded May 1, 2023 for a younger spouse/partner, live-in caregivers, legacy residents and children in defined care cases. No Fort Langley townhouse complex in is verified as 55+ — the village's 55+ building is the Waterfront apartment condo, cross-referenced above.

Secondary suites: capped at 120 m²: Township reporting on its suite rules records the maximum allowable gross floor area for a secondary suite at 120 m², and Council's 2025 direction extended suites to ground-oriented housing types including townhouses and fee-simple rowhouses — inside a strata townhouse, the registered bylaws must also allow it, and parking requirements apply.

Coach houses: a fee-simple second unit, never strata: Under Zoning Bylaw No. 2500, s. 102, a coach house is a second dwelling unit on a fee-simple lot — it is part of the same fee-simple title as the principal house, not a separate strata lot, and it cannot be sold separately from that lot. Do not price or market a Fort Langley coach house as strata product. (Standing correction for this run; zoning framework

ALR edges — stratification is barred and farm thresholds are three-tiered: Farm land on the village edges is in the ALR in places. ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09, s. 6; Strata Property Act, s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act, s. 21(1)) — an acreage-edge "townhouse strata" on ALR land is not a lawful form. The ALC also permits one additional residence without an ALC application where its size rules are met — up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less and up to 186 m² on properties more than 40 ha — subject to Township bylaws. Farm-class qualification itself is three-tiered ($2,500 of farm income on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the area over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha) — a flat "$2,500+" statement is an error.

Flood — a townhouse issue here, not just a house issue: Fort Langley is low-lying: the Township states the Salmon River Pump Station provides flood protection for the Fort Langley community and its flood box gates close when Fraser River levels rise. Parcel-level floodplain status for a specific complex: Not verified — get it from the Township, and for strata units check the insurance summary on the Form B for flood coverage and deductible terms.

Presales and assignments — REDMA: The 1912 presale requires a disclosure statement; REDMA s. 21 gives 7 days from the later of signing or acknowledging receipt of it to rescind, and s. 18 requires deposits to be held in trust. Assignment rights are contract-specific — assume none unless the contract and disclosure statement grant them.

items.t: "Bedford Landing" is a tenure trap, not a building. The same community name covers a 55+ apartment condo (Waterfront, BCS3620), an all-ages apartment condo (The Village, EPS998), an 11-unit live/work strata (Flatiron) and fee-simple non-strata row homes. A listing that says only "Bedford Landing" has told you nothing about tenure, age rules or who maintains the roof — the civic address and the title tell you.

The newest village housing project is a heritage restoration with three townhomes. The 1912, by Lanstone Homes (the same builder as Lily Terrace), is a presale collection of three heritage-inspired townhomes plus the restored 1912 George Albion Towle House, with pre-sales stated as coming Winter 2027 and move-in Fall 2027 — developer-stated timing, at village scale, and its tenure is not stated by the developer source.

The Township's SSMUH framework (Bylaw 6020, November 18, 2024) allows up to 4 units on eligible lots in the zones it amended, so a 6-plex is not available in the village, and the heritage framework would still apply.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Fort Langley
What trades here

items.t: Village fee-simple lots (the default form): The established village stock is freehold houses on fee-simple lots under the Fort Langley Community Plan and Zoning Bylaw No. 2500; downtown-core lots also sit inside the Heritage Conservation Area. Village residential zoning includes R-1E, named for the village in a Township public-hearing document; minimum lot areas and frontages for the village zones are not verified from a readable Bylaw No. 2500 section — no lot-size figure is invented here.

Bedford Landing — the fee-simple lot fabric (the named land angle for this area): Bedford Landing, on Billy Brown Road along the Bedford Channel, is a mixed master community built on the former McDonald Cedar Mill lands (mill opened 1921, 88-acre riverfront property): fee-simple row homes on their own lots (recorded as Row House (Non-Strata), built 2007) sit alongside strata buildings (The Village, EPS998; Waterfront, BCS3620; Flatiron live/work strata).: the row-home fabric is fee-simple; the strata buildings are separate — tenure is read address by address, because the community name alone tells a land buyer nothing about whether a parcel is a fee-simple lot or a strata lot. No Bedford Landing lot count or lot size is published in the sources checked: Not confirmed.

Acreage-edge lots (south and east): Acreage lots sit on the village edges, mainly south and east toward the Salmon River valley; farm land on the village edges is in the ALR in places — confirm a parcel on the ALC maps before valuing any farm, coach-house or subdivision angle.
No bare-land strata verified: Where a Fort Langley home is strata, it is a building strata (condo/townhouse) under the Strata Property Act — not a bare-land strata lot.

Serviced versus unserviced — it splits by fabric: the village and Bedford Landing are serviced urban ground; on the acreage edges, wells and septic are the diligence track. Well reports are due within 90 days of constructing, altering or decommissioning a well, and wells are searchable in the provincial GWELLS system; onsite sewage follows Fraser Health filing rules through an authorized person (record of sewerage system before construction, letter of certification after). Which specific edge parcels are on well/septic versus municipal services is not confirmed per parcel — pull the GWELLS record and the Fraser Health filings.

Floodplain ground: Fort Langley is low-lying: the Township states the Salmon River Pump Station provides flood protection for the Fort Langley community and its flood box gates close when Fraser River levels rise. Parcel-level floodplain mapping: Not verified — get it from the Township for the specific lot. Low ground is a land characteristic here, not a building detail.

Land assemblies / development sites: No land assembly is named as such in the Fort Langley research. The Township projects documented are civic, not lot inventory: salishan Place by the River (23430 Mavis Ave) and the Salmon River Pump Station upgrades. Nothing is presented here as for-sale development land beyond the lot fabrics above.
Market context, labelled as such: SnapStats covers Langley but has no land category (Detached vs "Condos & Townhomes" combined only). No detached figure here is a land figure.

items.t: Nearby areas: Walnut Grove (west/southwest), Langley City and the rest of the Township (south), and Maple Ridge across the Fraser River via the Golden Ears Bridge route.

Where the land actually differs: three fabrics — the heritage village grid around Glover Road (fee-simple village lots, many inside the Heritage Conservation Area), Bedford Landing on Billy Brown Road along the Bedford Channel (a planned enclave where fee-simple lots and strata buildings share one community name), and acreage edges mainly south and east toward the Salmon River valley, where ALR ground begins.
Glover Road is the village commercial street; Lee's Market, the village grocery, is at 23320 Mavis Avenue, and there is no shopping centre in Fort Langley.

Transit is a single bus: TransLink route 562 through the village on Glover Road between Langley Centre and Carvolth Exchange, via Walnut Grove. No SkyTrain or West Coast Express station is in Fort Langley — a material fact for any density claim made for village land.

SD35 schools physically in the village: Fort Langley Elementary (8877 Bartlett St) and Langley Fine Arts School (9096 Trattle St), a district K–12 fine arts choice school; a locator run for 8877 Bartlett St returned Fort Langley Elementary and D.W. Poppy Secondary, with no middle school shown. Catchments are address-based.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Fort Langley

items.t: Village plan: Fort Langley Community Plan, Township of Langley Bylaw No. 2527: (adopted October 26, 1987, as an amendment to the Township Official Community Plan) — the governing plan for village land.

Heritage Conservation Area (Bylaw 3710, October 27, 1997): The plan designates a Heritage Conservation Area under the Local Government Act covering the downtown core, to protect heritage character; non-exempt work requires heritage approval, with exemptions including minor additions under 50 m² that do not front a road (other than a lane) and conform to the guidelines. For a land buyer this is a buildability rule: what can be built or altered on a core lot is heritage-gated before it is zoning-gated.

Design controls on top of zoning: A Development Permit Area (Bylaw 3204, May 3, 1993) and the Fort Langley Design Guidelines (Bylaw 5063, April 28, 2014) also cover the village; the Building Façade Design Guidelines are non-binding policy.

Zoning: Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw No. 2500: R-1E is named for the village; the Bedford Landing strata buildings sit in site-specific CD zones (the Waterfront's is CD-55 — a zone number, not an age designation). Village zone minimum lot areas/frontages: Not verified from a readable bylaw section — never filled in here.

Secondary suites: capped at 120 m²: of gross floor area under Township rules, with Council's 2025 direction extending suites to ground-oriented housing including fee-simple rowhouses; parking requirements apply.

Coach houses: fee-simple s. 102 units, never strata: Under Zoning Bylaw No. 2500, s. 102, a coach house is a second dwelling unit on a fee-simple lot, part of the same title as the principal house, and cannot be sold separately. A live s. 102 text with the Township before relying on a coach-house angle for a specific lot. (Standing correction for this run; framework

Subdivision + servicing requirements (Township): A subdivision angle on a village or edge lot must be scoped with the Township (Approving Officer process, heritage/design overlays and flood/ALR status first) before any value is placed on it.

ALR rules (edge parcels): Residences on ALR land cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)). Subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval. Residence caps as the ALC states them: principal residence ≤500 m²; a secondary suite within the principal residence only; one additional residence without an ALC application up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less and up to 186 m² on properties over 40 ha, subject to Township bylaws.

BC Assessment farm class — full three-tier form: Gross annual value of at least $2,500 (farm area 0.8–4 ha); $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha (>4 ha); $10,000 (<0.8 ha); application delivered to the assessor on or before October 31. A flat "$2,500+" statement is an error and is not used here — it matters on Fort Langley's edges because an acreage lot priced on "farm status" must actually meet the tier for its size.

Well / septic diligence (acreage edges): GWELLS search for the well record (reports due within 90 days of well work) and Fraser Health authorized-person filings for onsite sewerage (record before construction, letter of certification after).

Bare-land strata — the form (no Fort Langley instance verified): If a lot WERE bare-land strata, it would be strata tenure — Form B, fees and bylaws on the lot. The BC block: Form B within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page; depreciation reports every 5 years for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions). For Fort Langley's fee-simple lots there is no strata, no Form B and no strata fee — title covenants/building scheme plus municipal rules govern instead.

Property transfer tax (PTT): First-Time Home Buyers': no PTT on the first $500,000 (maximum $8,000) at $835,000 or less, partial to $860,000 — relief turns on a qualifying home. Newly Built Home Exemption: full relief to $1,100,000, partial to $1,150,000. Township taxes were due July 2, 2026, with 5% penalties after July 2 and again after September 3, 2026, and utilities are now billed separately.

blocks.text: Good to know about Fort Langley

items.t: "Bedford Landing" is a tenure trap for land buyers too, not just home buyers. One community name covers fee-simple lots/row homes and three strata buildings on a former mill site — a lot listing that says only "Bedford Landing" has told you nothing about title, fees or who maintains what. The address and the Land Title record decide.
Heritage approval can outrank zoning on a core lot. Price core land on the heritage path, not just the zone.
Bylaw 6020 allows up to 4 units on an eligible Township lot; there is no 6-unit tier.

The Salmon River Pump Station provides the community's protection, its gates close as Fraser levels rise, and upgrades are in detailed design/tendering — a lot's protection story is municipal infrastructure plus the parcel's own flood information, not a seller's assurance.

faq.q: How many condo buildings are there in Fort Langley, really?
faq.a: Three verified apartment-condo buildings: The Village at Bedford Landing (23285 Billy Brown Rd, 2012), Waterfront at Bedford Landing (23215 Billy Brown Rd, 2009) and Lily Terrace (23189 Francis Ave, 2018–2019). Everything else attached in the village is townhouses or houses.

faq.q: Is Waterfront at Bedford Landing really 55+?
faq.a: Current listings say yes — "Ages 55+" and a "55+ community." A 55+ bylaw is legal in BC (it is the only age bylaw form left), but it restricts who may live there, not who may buy, and exemptions exist for a younger spouse/partner, live-in caregivers and legacy residents. Confirm the registered bylaw and your own position on the Form B.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Bedford Landing condo?
faq.a: Long-term rental bans are void in BC since Nov 24, 2022, and a building-data source records The Village at Bedford Landing as rentals allowed. In the 55+ Waterfront building, a tenant would still have to satisfy the age bylaw or an exemption, and short-term rentals can still be restricted.

faq.q: What do the strata fees cover, and what is the deductible risk in a riverside building?
faq.a: The Form B states the fee, the CRF balance and a summary of the strata's insurance. In a low-lying riverside location, read that insurance summary for flood-related coverage and the deductible amounts, and match them to your own unit-owner policy — the specific deductible figures for these buildings are not confirmed from a public source.

faq.q: Should I worry about levies in the 2009 and 2012 buildings?
faq.a: Those are the questions the depreciation report answers: every strata of five or more lots must now have one renewed every five years, with 30-year cost projections and three CRF funding models. Compare the CRF balance on the Form B against the report's near-term items (envelope, decks, parkade membrane) before deciding a unit is cheap or expensive.

faq.q: How many townhouse complexes are there in Fort Langley, really?
faq.a: Two verified strata complexes (Leah, 41 homes, 2024; Flatiron, 11 live/work units, 2012), plus fee-simple non-strata row homes at Bedford Landing, plus a 3-home presale (The 1912). The village's three apartment buildings are condos, not townhouses.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Bedford Landing row home and a Leah townhouse?
faq.a: Tenure. A Bedford Landing row home recorded as Row House (Non-Strata) is fee-simple: your lot, your title, no strata fee, no Form B, no depreciation report — and no strata to maintain the roof or envelope either. Leah is freehold strata: monthly fees, bylaws, a Form B and shared common property. Two homes on the same street can sit on opposite tracks.

faq.q: Can I run a business from a Flatiron unit?
faq.a: The complex is recorded as live/work, built by Parklane — but "live/work" in a listing is not a business licence. Check the strata bylaws, the CD zoning's permitted uses and the Township's business-licence requirements for your specific use before subjects.

faq.q: Is there a duplex development in Fort Langley I can buy into?
faq.a: A duplex purchase here is an individual building on a single lot, verified on its title.

faq.q: Is a Bedford Landing row home a half duplex?
faq.a: No. The row homes are recorded as Row House (Non-Strata) — complete dwellings on their own fee-simple lots, with no strata corporation, no Form B and no strata fee. A half duplex is one half of a two-unit building sold separately, either as a 2-lot strata or on a subdivided fee-simple lot; the row-home record is neither.

faq.q: What should I ask about flooding before buying a duplex here?
faq.a: The village is low-lying by the Fraser and Salmon Rivers; the Township says the Salmon River Pump Station provides flood protection and its flood box gates close when Fraser River levels rise.

faq.q: Do I need a heritage permit to renovate a house in the village?
faq.a: If the property is in the downtown-core Heritage Conservation Area designated in the Fort Langley Community Plan, alterations that are not exempt must follow the heritage rules — the plan's purpose is to protect the downtown's heritage character, and its exemptions cover items like minor additions under 50 m² that do not front a road and conform to the guidelines. Confirm the property's status with the Township.

faq.q: Which schools are in Fort Langley?
faq.a: For the sample address 8877 Bartlett Street, the SD35 School Locator returns Fort Langley Elementary and D.W. Poppy Secondary, with no middle school shown; Fort Langley Elementary at 8877 Bartlett Street and Langley Fine Arts School at 9096 Trattle Street are physically in the village. Other addresses may fall in different catchments.

faq.q: Is Fort Langley in a floodplain?
faq.a: The village is low-lying by the Fraser and Salmon Rivers; the Township states the Salmon River Pump Station provides flood protection for the Fort Langley community when Fraser River levels rise. Check parcel flood information with the Township before purchase.
